text:
devon: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/45123 — adds adaptive prefetch backoff + routing rule that prefers low-latency pools. Need runtime + infra + security eyes before I can schedule a canary. Can someone own reviews?

sam: quick skim looks reasonable but tagging infra for eviction config + gating.

anya: I can take runtime review. Are there perf numbers or a short test I can run?

devon: thanks @anya. local microbench results attached in PR (short): median token latency ~1.8ms on p4 with synthetic seq=64. Test command I used:
```
./scripts/run_local_bench.sh --model=llama2 --seq=64 --reps=100
```
Also the change adds a feature flag: "prefetch_adaptive" in runtime config.

carl: assigning myself for infra review. I'll check the eviction policy diff and confirm there's no change to kube node selectors or storage paths. If it touches configstore KMS, ping me.

devon: it does add a tiny config key under /ops/runtime/eviction/prefetch_adaptive (yaml), no KMS changes. Diff snippet in PR: 
```
- prefetch: false
+ prefetch: 
+   adaptive: true
+   window_ms: 250
```

rita: security here. Quick question: does this surface any new authz or header propagation to external services? If not I can do async pass.

devon: no external calls; it's internal routing and cache behavior only.

deploy-bot: Canary window available: Tue 22:00 UTC — uses canary cohort 2. Reply "schedule" to reserve.

anya: runtime note — prefer to ship with adaptive prefetch disabled by default in prod and enable via runtime flag during canary. Can we default to off?

devon: yep — switched default to off and introduced flag `--enable-prefetch-adaptive` (off by default). Pushed new commit.

carl: infra LGTM after the gating check. Two tiny nits in YAML formatting, I pushed a follow-up.

rita: security LGTM — no authz surface.

anya: runtime LGTM with the flag default-off change. Suggest we run the canary for 4 hours and monitor latency and evictions.

devon: scheduled canary for Tue 22:00 UTC (reserved). Will watch metrics and share dashboards in the PR. If canary looks good I'll request merge slot Wed 14:00 UTC. Thanks all.

sam: thanks! Reply here if you want me to run any extra synthetic traces during canary.

devon: will do — appreciate the help.
